title: Extending Maximum Age of Vocational Driving Licences for Drivers Certified Medically Fit
what_it_is: Extending Maximum Age of Vocational Driving Licences for Drivers Certified Medically Fit

sections.label: Vocational licence age limit study
sections.summary: LTA commissioned SMA to study raising the 75-year vocational licence age limit; SMA recommended against it, and LTA decided not to raise it for now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) recently commissioned the Singapore Medical Association (SMA) to conduct a study on a possible increase in the statutory age limit of 75 years old for holding a vocational licence (VL) to drive a public service vehicle.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Based on past accident statistics and SMA's medical assessment, SMA recommends not to increase the age limit for vocational licence holders beyond 75 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For instance, taxi and PHC drivers in the 70 to 74 age group were five to six times more likely to have had an accident, compared to taxi and PHC drivers aged below 60.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Given safety concerns, LTA has assessed and considered SMA's recommendations and decided not to raise the maximum age limit for vocational licence holders for now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: But older drivers aged 50 to 74 can continue to hold valid vocational licences if they undergo regular check-ups and meet the necessary medical requirements.

sections.label: Taxi driver age limit extensions
sections.summary: The statutory age limit for taxi drivers rose from 70 to 73 in 2006 and to 75 in 2012, with over-70 VL holders a minority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, we extended the statutory age limit for taxi drivers from 70 years to 73 years in 2006, and then again, from 73 years to 75 years in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In addition, as at August 2022, the number of VL holders aged over 70 remains a minority of between 1% and 5%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As regard to the Member's suggestions about time-restricted routes, as well as hours of operation, this is something we will carefully consider in our future review, taking note that there are challenges and implications in administrating, as well as in enforcing such limited, or time-bound and route-bound licence.
